own_solution.law: Infinite square well E_n = n^2 (hc)^2 / (8 mc^2 L^2); photon lambda = hc / (E_4 - E_1) = 8 mc^2 L^2 / (15 hc)
assumptions: non-relativistic particle in an ideal infinite well
single photon carries the full level difference
L = 0.5 nm at the moment of the transition

notes: E1 = 1537600/(8*511000*0.25) = 1.5045 eV; dE = 15 E1 = 22.568 eV; lambda = 1240/22.568 = 54.946 nm. With L = 0.5 + 2.4 = 2.9 nm, lambda scales by (2.9/0.5)^2 = 33.64 -> 1848.4 nm. For the R sentences I assume the electron stays in the n = 4 level while the well is widened (adiabatic widening keeps n), then makes the 4 -> 1 transition; this is the natural reading. Widening after the emission (TEDF7, T6BE7) cannot affect the already emitted photon; widening the separate dot (T7B70, T425C) has no path to the well. T425C and T6BE7 say 'a small amount' rather than 2.4 nm; they do not change the answer, but as variants they do not state the same number as the others.
